rationale: The distribution-shift meta-principle establishes that performance under a test distribution different from the training distribution is not guaranteed and requires assumptions; the observed lower performance of LLM evaluators on OOD data is a specific manifestation of this general boundary. The meta-principle bounds the expectation of OOD evaluation capability without asserting the exact drop, leaving the empirical magnitude to the study.
